title: Quality Evaluator
what: A Python script that acts as a judge: you give it an output (a support reply, text generated by another AI, a summary, a translation) and a list of criteria you wrote, and it evaluates it criterion by criterion with the Anthropic API, returning a structured JSON verdict: pass or fail, a score per criterion, evidence for every failure, and what to fix. It's the piece that turns "it sounds fine to me" into a repeatable review, and the foundation for automatically monitoring the quality of any AI-driven process you're running.
forWho: For anyone already generating content or replies with AI (from any provider or team) who needs quality control that doesn't depend on reading everything by hand. It pays off as soon as you produce more text than you can review: you evaluate everything automatically and people only look at the failures and a sample of the passes.
capabilities: Evaluates an output against your criteria, one by one, with a 0-10 score and cited evidence for each
Returns a global JSON verdict (pass / fail / needs_review) computed by your code from the scores, not by the model's whim
Accepts criteria as a plain text file: you change them without touching code
Distinguishes disqualifying criteria (a zero there fails everything) from weighted quality criteria
Uses claude-sonnet-5 as the judge, a strong model, because judging well is harder than writing
limits: Doesn't fact-check against the real world: it judges the output against your criteria and the context you pass it, not against the internet
Doesn't fully replace human review: the fails and a sample of the passes should still go through people
Isn't a perfectly neutral judge: AI judges have biases (they favor long, confident-sounding text); measure its agreement with you before trusting it
Doesn't evaluate code by running it or websites by browsing them: it judges text; for code, tests are a better judge

README.md
files.content:
# Quality Evaluator

Judges any text (support replies, AI-generated content, summaries) against YOUR criteria and returns a JSON verdict with a score per criterion, evidence, and suggested fixes.

## Installation

```bash
pip install anthropic
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-key"
```

## Usage

1. Write your criteria in `criterios.txt`, one per line. Ones starting with `!` are disqualifying:

```
! Does not invent data that isn't in the context
! Treats the customer respectfully at all times
Answers everything that's asked
Warm, professional tone
Under 150 words
```

2. Evaluate:

```bash
python evaluador.py --salida respuesta.txt --criterios criterios.txt --contexto pregunta.txt
```

Output:

```json
{
  "veredicto": "revisar",
  "nota_media": 6.4,
  "eliminatorio_suspendido": false,
  "criterios": [
    {"criterio": "Answers everything that's asked", "nota": 4,
     "evidencia": "Does not answer the second question ('can I change the date?')",
     "mejora": "Add the answer about changing the date", "eliminatorio": false}
  ],
  "resumen": "Correct in tone but incomplete: leaves a question unanswered."
}
```

The exit code lets you chain without parsing: `0` pass, `2` needs review, `3` fail.

```bash
python evaluador.py --salida r.txt --criterios c.txt || echo "send to human review"
```

## Two design decisions that matter

- **The model scores, your code decides.** The verdict comes from fixed rules in `veredicto_final()` (average, thresholds, disqualifiers), not from the model's mood. Adjust the `NOTA_APTO` and `NOTA_REVISAR` thresholds to your taste.
- **The criteria are a text file.** Anyone on the team can tune them without touching Python. Concrete criteria evaluate better: "under 150 words" works; "be good" doesn't.

## Calibrate the judge before trusting it

Take 15 outputs a person has already judged and compare verdicts. If the judge passes things you'd fail, tighten the criteria (or split a vague one into two concrete ones) and repeat. An uncalibrated judge is an opinion with JSON formatting.

## For production

- Evaluate EVERYTHING automatically; people review the `no_apto`, the `revisar`, and 1 in 10 `apto`.
- Save the JSON outputs with a date: the trend of `nota_media` over time is your free quality metric.
- If you're evaluating thousands of outputs, ask Claude Code to adapt it to the Batch API (50% cheaper, no rush).

setup.title: Set up the environment
setup.action: pip install anthropic (Python 3.9+; the script uses list[dict], available since 3.9).
setup.expect: python -c "import anthropic" runs with no errors.

setup.title: Export your key
setup.action: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..." with the key from console.anthropic.com.
setup.expect: echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY shows it in the terminal you'll use.

setup.title: Save the script and write your criteria
setup.action: Copy evaluador.py into your project and create criterios.txt with 4-6 real criteria, marking disqualifiers with !. Be specific: each criterion, one single checkable thing.
setup.expect: python evaluador.py --help shows the help text and criterios.txt exists.

setup.title: First evaluation
setup.action: Save a real text you want to judge in respuesta.txt (and its originating request in pregunta.txt, if you have it) and run: python evaluador.py --salida respuesta.txt --criterios criterios.txt --contexto pregunta.txt
setup.expect: The JSON with a score per criterion, cited evidence, verdict, and summary.
setup.stuck: If a criterion gets odd scores, it's almost always because the criterion is vague: split it into two concrete ones.

setup.title: Calibrate against your own judgment
setup.action: Evaluate 15 outputs a person has already classified as good or bad and compare verdicts with theirs.
setup.expect: High agreement (12-13 of 15 or more). If not, adjust criteria and thresholds and repeat: you're training the judge, not the other way around.

setup.title: Connect it to your pipeline
setup.action: Use the exit code (0/2/3) or the JSON to route: pass continues on its way, needs-review and fail go to a human queue. Save the JSON outputs with a date.
setup.expect: Continuous quality control without reading everything, with metrics you can show.

test.name: Normal run
test.input: A correct support reply evaluated against your criteria.
test.expect: verdict pass, high scores with cited evidence, and exit code 0.

test.name: Disqualifying failure
test.input: An output that invents a fact, with the criterion "! Does not invent data" in the list.
test.expect: verdict fail even if the average is high, eliminatorio_suspendido true, and evidence pointing to the invented fact.

test.name: Gray area
test.input: A mediocre output: polite but incomplete.
test.expect: verdict needs-review with an average score between 5 and 7 and concrete fixes on the weak criteria.

test.name: Empty criteria
test.input: A criterios.txt with only comments (#) or empty.
test.expect: Clear error "has no criteria" without spending an API call.

credentials.name: Anthropic API
credentials.how: Key in the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable, never in the script or the repository.
credentials.cost: Pay per token; an evaluation with claude-sonnet-5 costs around a cent, depending on length

risks: An uncalibrated judge mistaken for an oracle: it passes garbage with a pretty format. Mitigation: calibration with 15 human-judged cases is part of setup, and repeats whenever criteria change.
AI judge biases: it favors long, confident text. Mitigation: the prompt warns against this and concrete criteria constrain it; watch whether long texts systematically score better.
Optimizing for the judge instead of for the customer: the team learns to satisfy the criteria, not to work better. Mitigation: review the criteria every quarter against real customer complaints.
Evaluating outputs that contain sensitive data. Mitigation: same rules as always: anonymize whatever shouldn't travel to the API and check your account's retention policy.

examples.name: Weekly batch
examples.prompt: for f in salidas/*.txt; do python evaluador.py --salida "$f" --criterios criterios.txt > "informes/$(basename $f .txt).json"; done

examples.name: Monitor another agent
examples.prompt: Chain it with the classifier or the extractor from this catalog: every generated output goes through evaluador.py and only the passes continue without human review.
